entries.title: The Silent Consensus
entries.summary: Dean Ball, Head of Strategic Futures at OpenAI, examines how more capable AI could reshape society and how people can retain control of their institutions.

entries.title: Research acceleration: The jagged frontier
entries.summary: OpenAI measures how coding agents are accelerating AI research, where their performance remains uneven, and what this signals about recursive self-improvement.

entries.title: How Sumitomo Life’s leaders helped teams adopt ChatGPT Enterprise
entries.summary: Sumitomo Life uses ChatGPT Enterprise to research insurers, prepare proposals, and draft code for investment analysis. Early use by executives helped drive adoption.

entries.title: Inside the Codex sandbox
entries.summary: See how Codex runs commands on your machine while enforcing the filesystem and network limits you control across macOS, Linux, and Windows.

entries.title: Managing frontier AI risk: From training to deployment
entries.summary: OpenAI explains how it manages frontier AI risk from training through deployment with model alignment, sandboxing, blocking safeguards, and monitoring.

entries.title: Le Groupe Figaro and OpenAI partner to bring Le Figaro journalism to ChatGPT
entries.summary: Le Groupe Figaro and OpenAI partner to bring Le Figaro’s journalism to ChatGPT through summaries and excerpts, with links to original stories.

entries.title: Advancing chip design with OpenAI models
entries.summary: OpenAI models optimized circuits used in Jalapeño silicon and improved RISC‑V core designs, showing progress in AI-assisted chip design with GPT‑6 Astra.

entries.title: v2.1.328
entries.summary:
- [Other] Added auto mode for Claude Opus 4.6 and Sonnet 4.6 on Amazon Bedrock, Google Cloud's Agent Platform, Microsoft Foundry and Claude apps gateway; interactive sessions with no permission mode start in it
- [Other] Added "onFailure": "block" for mcp_tool hooks, as for command and HTTP hooks: a hook whose call fails blocks the action
- [Other] Added a warning when a message from a session that skips permission prompts may be held and dropped by a cloud session
- [Other] Added a notice in /status and claude doctor when an OpenTelemetry exporter has no endpoint and its data would likely be lost
- [Other] Added CLAUDE_CODE_DISABLE_DEFERRED_TOOL_RESUME, which lets a host stop claude -p --resume and --continue from running a tool call that a hook deferred
- [Other] Added support for apps that embed Claude Code to switch on the policy plugin's allowManagedModsOnly option; an admin's managed settings still win
- [Other] Added a startup warning to the Claude apps gateway when a policy's maxEffortLevel is not a valid effort level
- [Other] Self-hosted runner: Added --repository-folder to name the folder that sessions use for a repository at --capacity 1, in place of its path under the base folder, which can't be a symbolic link
- [Other] Self-hosted runner: Added a start-up warning when the host's settings.json sets a default permission mode that sessions ignore
- [Other] Self-hosted runner: Added --hook-label to claude self-hosted-runner orchestrator, to hand chosen session labels to the spawn-runner hook
- [Other] Self-hosted runner: Added --metadata key=value to claude --environment, to label a session for the spawn-runner hook
- [Other] Self-hosted runner: Added claude_code_self_hosted_orchestrator_session_queue_wait_by_reason_seconds to the orchestrator's /metrics, so a re-opened session's wait can be told from a new one's
- [Other] Self-hosted runner: Added an orchestrator metric, claude_code_self_hosted_orchestrator_sessions_given_up_total, that counts by cause how often Anthropic gave up starting a runner for a session
- [Other] Fixed Bash commands in zsh stopping with a "not found" error at a word that starts with =, such as echo ==== or [ a == b ]; =cmd no longer expands to a command's path
- [Other] Fixed automatic compaction reusing the session's earlier system prompt instead of rebuilding it the way /compact does
- [Other] Fixed markdown rendering freezing on some very long or malformed input
- [Other] Fixed rare screen freezes
- [Other] Fixed Esc often being lost at a permission prompt or question when you typed straight after it; in terminals that send Alt as Esc and a key, an unused Alt or Option key now declines there
- [Other] Fixed a paste or a terminal's reply being typed into the prompt when a slow connection cut it in two
- [Other] Fixed saving a scheduled task erasing the project's other saved tasks when the scheduled tasks file can't be read, on third-party providers or with telemetry or feature flags turned off
- [Other] Fixed a scheduled task with a typo in the project's scheduled tasks file being deleted the next time that file was saved
- [Other] Fixed a case where a resumed cloud session could lose its compaction summary or recent messages when a message was saved late
- [Other] Fixed the token counts on the spinner and for subagents counting a retried reply twice, missing replies that were not streamed, and standing still while Claude thinks
- [Other] Fixed the error shown when usage credits run out mid-response, which named a rate limit
- [Other] Fixed auto mode failing every turn outside Claude Desktop with CLAUDE_CODE_DISABLE_EXPERIMENTAL_BETAS set behind a gateway rejecting betas, on Bedrock, Agent Platform, Foundry or Claude apps gateway
- [Other] Fixed CLAUDE_STREAM_IDLE_TIMEOUT_MS not lengthening the 5-minute connection limit on gateways, custom base URLs and cloud providers
- [Other] Fixed some Claude Desktop sessions on third-party providers, other than scheduled tasks, ending for good with "Prompt is too long" after large tool results; the largest are now left out
- [Other] Fixed MCP tools whose input schema starts with anyOf, oneOf or allOf going missing on third-party providers or with telemetry or feature flags turned off
- [Other] Fixed an MCP tool with an invalid input schema failing requests on third-party providers or with telemetry or feature flags turned off; the tool is now left out and Claude is told why
- [Other] Fixed effort being turned off for a subagent's model for the session if Bedrock, Google Cloud's Agent Platform or Foundry refused its progress summary's effort setting (regression in 2.1.327)
- [Other] Fixed Code Mode stopping a script when a permission prompt outside auto or bypass mode, a plan approval or a question stayed open for ten minutes
- [Other] Fixed Code Mode scripts in auto and bypass-permissions modes failing to call an MCP server that had connected while the previous script was running
- [Other] Fixed Code Mode scripts not running in the background in auto or bypass permissions mode in a session chosen in the claude --resume picker
- [Other] Fixed Code Mode losing a loaded skill, hook context or a note typed with a permission approval when resuming a session in which one reply ran several scripts
- [Other] Fixed Claude not being told that a Code Mode script was cut off when the session was resumed from the picker or in a mode that asks for permission
- [Other] Fixed Code Mode silently using undefined for top-level variables that an earlier failed script never set
- [Other] Fixed Code Mode scripts not being told when a failing command's long output was cut
- [Other] Fixed Code Mode refusing valid scripts that start with a { block
- [Other] Fixed Code Mode refusing scripts that use both a top-level await and a top-level return
- [Other] Fixed an @-mentioned small file not being attached in Code Mode after a script had read or written it
- [Other] Fixed Code Mode offering write() and edit() to read-only subagents that can't call them
- [Other] Fixed Claude starting a turn by itself in Code Mode when Esc was followed by a command such as /model
- [Other] Fixed Claude in Code Mode not being told to run workflows only when you ask, or the workflow size you set in /config
- [Other] Fixed Remote Control repeating the same disconnect message, and telling you to retry a session that can't reconnect
- [Other] Fixed a waiting permission prompt being lost, and its answer ignored, when a remote session restarted while the service was slow
- [Other] Fixed cloud sessions resuming a cleared conversation after a rewind followed by /clear
- [Other] Fixed a remote session losing a turn's tool calls and results when its runner or worker was lost after a dropped model stream had been retried
- [Other] Fixed cloud and Remote Control sessions that just started, or have an @ in their title, being unreachable in cross-session messaging from a session with Remote Control on
- [Other] Fixed Claude being told that cloud sessions can never reply; it now learns when a reply can come and how else to get the result
- [Other] Fixed /diff, the Changes pane of Remote Control sessions and the diff beside an edit leaving out committed work after a command moved into another repository
- [Other] Fixed Remote Control not showing a running workflow's agents when a session run by an IDE extension or other SDK app is opened over an hour after the workflow last made progress
- [Other] Remote Control: Fixed an idle Desktop or VS Code session showing as running after Remote Control is turned on
- [Other] Fixed the model saying background agents were still running after an SDK interrupt had stopped them
- [Other] Fixed Send now in the desktop app and SDK hosts telling Claude that a stopped web search found no results
- [Other] Fixed Cmd+letter being typed into the prompt in terminals that report Cmd
- [Other] Fixed Ctrl+click opening a link twice in GNOME Terminal, side mouse buttons acting as clicks, and the first wheel notch in the other direction being ignored after a pause, in fullscreen mode
- [Other] Fixed Shift+Enter in Konsole outside tmux and ssh, and Alt shortcuts on non-Latin keyboard layouts in terminals that speak the kitty keyboard protocol
- [Other] Linux: Fixed pasting in other apps freezing while Claude Code is suspended with Ctrl+Z, when xclip or wl-copy is installed
- [Other] Linux: Fixed Ctrl+V missing the clipboard image, pasting an old one or hanging
- [Other] Fixed text copied in fullscreen mode including the quote bar, losing spaces at line wraps when a drag scrolled upward, or missing words under the "Jump to bottom" pill
- [Other] Fixed an image path pasted into a ! command becoming an attachment
- [Other] Fixed Ctrl+C showing no exit warning while the ? shortcuts list is open
- [Other] Fixed Ctrl+R search in fullscreen mode and the /theme color editor picking the wrong row when keys arrive together, and keys being dropped there and in the search of /config and /plugin
- [Other] Fixed wrong or missing colors inside GNU screen
- [Other] Fixed many background notifications cutting into the top border of open dialogs in fullscreen mode
- [Other] Fixed a message to a background agent showing a long file path in place of a pasted image
- [Other] Fixed /goal removing a skill's Stop hook, or ending early on another hook's result, when both had the same wording
- [Other] Fixed /bug saying cancelled after the report was sent
- [Other] Fixed Esc not dismissing the transcript share question for Pro and Max users
- [Other] Fixed /hooks losing your place when going back
- [Other] Fixed /export writing a file named .txt when the name was left empty
- [Other] Fixed /terminal-setup in Zed replacing a symlinked keymap.json with a plain file
- [Other] Fixed /install-github-app adding a code review workflow when asked to update the existing workflow file
- [Other] Fixed /plugin reopening a skill, or closing the open page, when a slow save or removal finished after you went back
- [Other] Fixed /plugin asking to uninstall the wrong plugin, or ignoring Esc, after leaving a plugin while a change was still running
- [Other] Fixed typing and arrow keys not working on the /plugin Installed tab after a search with no results or a click on the tab row
- [Other] Fixed holding Enter in /plugin turning off several installed plugins
- [Other] Fixed the /usage plugin total stopping at 2,000 tokens on 1M context models, and low token estimates in /usage and /plugin when no model is picked
- [Other] Fixed Esc on the Bedrock access keys step closing /login instead of going back
- [Other] Fixed /exit and Ctrl+D describing running work differently, and /exit warning about a workflow that had stopped
- [Other] Fixed Claude calling an artifact private after reading one in a shared folder or publishing to another organization's, and saying only named people can open one when its folder's people can too
- [Other] Fixed a plugin's toast sometimes showing another plugin's text
- [Other] Fixed a mod saved just after a turn began sometimes reloading mid-turn instead of at the turn's end
- [Other] Fixed one malformed OTEL_RESOURCE_ATTRIBUTES entry dropping the variable's other labels from metric points, events, and spans. Now only that entry is left off
- [Other] Fixed agent hooks running past their timeout while compacting after a request was refused as too large
- [Other] Fixed a crash at startup when FORCE_COLOR is set to a negative number
- [Other] Fixed a crash in secret masking when the machine is almost out of memory
- [Other] Fixed the Bash sandbox on Linux renaming .git/HEAD after each command when the branch name is not valid UTF-8
- [Other] Self-hosted runner: Fixed all running sessions being stopped when a proxy or web filter answered a poll with HTTP 200 and a body such as {}; the runner now retries such a poll
- [Other] Self-hosted runner: Fixed deletion of a kept clone's objects or refs, and of commits that existed only there, after a temporary disk error; that start now fails instead
- [Other] Fixed self-hosted runners stopping when their token ran out on a host whose clock is slow or was set back
- [Other] Self-hosted runner: Fixed sessions with Anthropic-managed git losing git access to GitHub after a script or hook in the session ran claude again
- [Other] Fixed self-hosted runners with Anthropic-managed git being unable to fetch or push where the machine's git config sets http.proactiveAuth
- [Other] Self-hosted runner: Fixed a runner that exited without telling the server when setup failed after it had registered; it now deregisters with a reason, and an on-demand runner reports the failed start
- [Other] Self-hosted runner: Fixed archiving or requeueing a session not taking effect while it waited for another session to prepare the same repository (--capacity above 1)
- [Other] Self-hosted runner: Fixed a session with a damaged .claude.json failing every later start under --trust-workspace false; it now starts on defaults, with MCP servers turned off there on again
- [Other] Self-hosted runner: Fixed a failed start's message losing the words that say what failed when a checkout hook or git printed a lot
- [Other] Fixed the self-hosted runner skipping its post-session hook when a disk stalled for a few seconds; on a dead disk a session's end can take 25 seconds longer by default
- [Other] Fixed self-hosted runners: a session that resumes in a new Claude config directory no longer loses its task list
- [Other] Fixed Claude not being told when a self-hosted session starts without one of its repositories, and why
- [Other] Self-hosted runner: Fixed --correlation-id of claude --environment not reaching the spawn-runner hook
- [Other] Fixed the self-hosted runner setup wizard's key rotation advice, which now warns that revoking a key stops the sessions running under it
- [Other] Improved claude -p and SDK sessions to fetch managed-settings plugins that have their own git repository, in the background, for a later session
- [Other] Improved how soon managed-settings plugins from a git marketplace load on a fresh machine in claude -p, SDK and Claude Desktop sessions; a short run may exit up to 30 seconds later
- [Other] Improved the time to resume large sessions
- [Other] Improved memory use when resuming a session with many images
- [Other] Improved memory use and response time in long SDK and desktop sessions that run slow commands or tools
- [Other] Improved Code Mode's speed in auto and bypass-permissions modes by removing a 0.75 second pause after most scripts
- [Other] Improved prompt caching for new Code Mode sessions that have MCP servers, and Claude is now told when a server is still connecting and when the list of servers changes
- [Other] Improved Code Mode's token use with shorter tool descriptions
- [Other] Improved Code Mode to show the command a script is running, and its output, while it runs
- [Other] Improved Code Mode edits: an edit that changes nothing no longer stops a script, and Claude is told where a failed edit matches or comes closest
- [Other] Improved Code Mode: Claude is now told which tool calls were still running when a script failed
- [Other] Improved how Claude starts dev servers in Code Mode's auto and bypass modes: Claude is told to run them as background tasks that show in /tasks
- [Other] Windows: Improved Code Mode by telling Claude that scripts' shell commands run in Git Bash and that PowerShell aliases run instead of functions with the same name
- [Other] Improved starting several in-process teammates at once: far fewer now fail with "Lock file is already being held"
- [Other] Improved the computer use approval dialog: it now shows each app's level of access and plainer warnings
- [Other] Improved cross-session messaging: Claude now explains that Remote Control is off when a cloud session or another computer is not listed
- [Other] Improved claude -p text output to say on stderr when a message from another session is held or dropped, and how to allow it
- [Other] Improved Claude's answers on who can open an artifact it published: Claude is now told to check the artifact again instead of repeating the last publish's answer
- [Other] Improved resumed self-hosted runner sessions: Claude now checks whether its earlier work is still there, and says what is missing
- [Other] Changed plan mode and Bash prompts for Opus 4.6 and Sonnet 4.6 on third-party providers to use and offer auto mode, as on newer models; disableAutoMode turns both off
- [Other] Changed Code Mode to no longer run UserPromptSubmit hooks, managed ones included, on scripts' output; to redact that output, use a PostToolUse hook with updatedToolOutput
- [Other] Changed /code-review on most models to report only bugs and CLAUDE.md violations; run /simplify for reuse, simplification and efficiency cleanups
- [Other] Changed /code-review to mark each finding Important, Pre-existing or Nit on most models, and to end each summary with a suggested fix; a clean review's list now reads "Code review found no issues."
- [Other] Changed deniedMcpServers entries of the form claude.ai <name> to apply to that connector in cloud and self-hosted runner sessions too
- [Other] Changed managed PostToolUse hooks to no longer fire for calls refused before they ran: no log entry, rewrite, block or stop there; PostToolBatch gets most, not marked as refused
- [Other] Changed /bug to ask Yes or No before sending, so repeated Enters no longer send a report or open GitHub
- [Other] Changed subagents in claude -p, the Agent SDK, desktop and VS Code to wait for their own subagents by default when CLAUDE_CODE_FORK_SUBAGENT=0 is set
- [Other] Changed claude -p with CLAUDE_CODE_FORK_SUBAGENT=0 to count a background subagent and those it waits for against one 10-minute wait; raise CLAUDE_CODE_PRINT_BG_WAIT_CEILING_MS for longer chains
- [Other] Changed a shell command rewritten by a PermissionRequest hook to a sandbox-excluded command to run outside the sandbox
- [Other] Changed the Claude in Chrome welcome screen and /chrome to say that Claude Code asks before Claude acts on a site, unless your permission mode or a rule in /permissions answers
- [Other] Changed Claude Desktop and Agent SDK sessions on third-party providers or with telemetry or feature flags off to end the turn when closed with a question open, instead of continuing without an answer
- [Other] Changed pasted text to be marked for Claude as pasted, on third-party providers or with telemetry or feature flags turned off
- [Other] Changed subagent progress summaries in terminal sessions on the Anthropic API to be written by the default small fast model from short notes, also with telemetry off, using far fewer tokens
- [Other] Changed how a sandbox that can't start is reported, unless sandbox.failIfUnavailable is set: the next sandboxed Bash command is refused and says that the sandbox is off for the session
- [Other] Changed /list-agents to show its list to you alone; Claude lists sessions itself when needed
- [Other] Self-hosted runner: Changed the built-in gh api to be off by default where settings guard Claude's GitHub tools by name; --use-anthropic-gh true turns it on
- [Other] Self-hosted runner: Changed a claude that a wrapper script runs before the session's own claude is up, or after it has ended, to have no Anthropic-managed git
- [Other] Self-hosted runner: Changed CLAUDE_RUNNER_SESSION_UUID and CLAUDE_CODE_REMOTE_SESSION_UUID to both be set for the session and its checkout, post-session and spawn-runner hooks
- [Other] Changed self-hosted runners at --capacity 1 to refuse a session earlier when the path of a repository it pushes to is a symbolic link
- [Other] [VSCode] Added a notice when a message from another session is held, with a link to the settings file that can allow it
- [Other] [VSCode] Fixed the permission prompt cutting off its No button, reply field or title when the panel is low or a command, URL or description is long
- [Other] [VSCode] Fixed failed or blocked tool calls showing no reason or a reason cut short, and Glob and Grep counting an error as results

entries.title: Data Contracts
entries.summary: Data contracts are a way to describe the contents and guarantees of datasets. Simon Harrer and Arif Wider describe in detail what they are and how to use them. They apply practices from API design to data by treating them as data-providing services - such as data products - whose interfaces we want to define as clearly as possible. This approach significantly increases the robustness of large-scale data landscapes, and gives both people and AI agents the explicit, trustworthy metadata they need to work with data autonomously, which is why more and more enterprises are adopting them. more…

entries.title: [AINews] GPT-6.2 Astra, the #2 Frontier Model is better and 20%-600% cheaper, but has mixed reviews; 6.2 Sol likely main workhorse
entries.summary: OpenAI shipped GPT-6.2 Astra and Sol today, two days before Anthropic’s expected first trading day. In Artificial Analysis’ tests, Sol ties September’s Astra at about 15% of the cost per task. New Astra scores 62 on the Intelligence Index, just behind Fable 5.2 at 65. Net net, Anthropic still owns the world’s best model, but OpenAI owns the world’s most efficient models in terms of intelligence per $. What’s more unusual about this launch is the STRONGLY negative influencer feedback… which prompted a defensive response… View post on X ↗ We think that some of this is overreacting and normal influencer tendency to either have everything be 🤯🤯🤯 or the literal WORST.MODEL.EVER, BUT also that some of the criticisms are valid, and the RL artefacts are noticeable and downright bizarre (don’t even get us started about the terrible launch video). However, we still use it to automate our work and that’s all that matters in the end. Great ship, but Anthropic’s IPO is unaffected and that will be probably the headline of the week/year/decade (until OpenAI IPO’s….) Today’s AI News is brought to you by SerpApi!Retrieve public web pages by URL as LLM-ready Markdown or structured JSON. Map sites and run bounded crawls with one API. Pair with 100+ SerpApi search APIs for search-to-content workflows. Check them out to support LS, and contact business@latent.space for feedback! AI Twitter RecapGPT-6.2 Astra and SolAvailability. Today’s models are rolling out to ChatGPT Work and Codex for Plus, Pro, Enterprise and Edu, and to developers through the API as gpt-6.2-astra and gpt-6.2-sol. OpenAIAPI prices per million tokens. Astra is $8 input, $0.40 cached input and $40 output. Sol keeps its predecessor’s pricing at $2, $0.10 and $10. Both have 1M context and a 128K output limit. Vals · Ultrafast pricing and rolloutAstra for Law. The Enterprise configuration adds a legal search index. Artificial Analysis measured 20.8% on Harvey LAB-AA, versus 15.0% for base Astra. Artificial AnalysisPreparedness. OpenAI rated Astra High for AI Self-Improvement, a first for one of its externally released models. On a separate measure, Vals’ RSI-Index rose from 27.07% to 29.01%, with 50% denoting its human reference. System card · ValsFrontierMath Erdős. Epoch verified seven solutions in Lean out of 68 problems. The previous best was three. EpochWhat the benchmarks measureAgents’ Last Exam 1.1. OpenAI reports Astra at xhigh gained 5.2 points over GPT-6 Astra at max, using less than a third of the cost per task. It reports a 5.5-point lead over Fable 5.2 at about 5% of the cost on that test. On GDPval v2, it says Astra used 22% fewer output tokens than its predecessor. OpenAI’s resultsLong engineering runs. Mercor’s OpenWorldEngineer puts Astra at 67.2%, Fable 5.2 at 54.6%, and GPT-6 Astra at 44.2%. On Vals’ multi-turn Vibe Code Bench, Astra was first and Sol was third. Mercor · Vals3D and robotics. Astra led AA-3D with 1,318, ahead of Fable at 1,271 and Sol at 1,259. On Artificial Analysis’s robotics preview, Astra scored 79 and Sol 78, ahead of Fable at 75. Artificial AnalysisResearch agents. On Perplexity’s WANDR, Astra scored 0.783 at about $12.54 per task. Sol reached 0.746 at about $2.65. PerplexityEarly testers disagreedMatt Shumer called the models “essentially unusable” after weeks of testing and said his Opus and Fable agents rejected much of Astra’s subagent work. Review · Workflow detailsPietro Schirano attributed many of his early issues to the harness. Arena’s Peter Gostev tested Astra against Fable on visual coding and singled out Astra’s SVG peacock. Schirano · GostevThe demos. Gabriel Chua built a walkable Singapore using more than 100 Codex threads. Simon Willison ran the same three.js mech prompt through several models, including Astra, Sol, Carbon and Fable. Singapore build · Same-prompt comparisonMicrosoft Ignite and GeminiMicrosoft ships its own coding models. MAI Code 2 is for multi-step coding, and Code 2 Flash is for quicker edits. Both are available in GitHub Copilot’s model picker, Copilot Fusion and Foundry. Microsoft also announced a multimodal upgrade to its Decision model. MicrosoftCopilot Fusion. Microsoft reports 71.2% on Terminal-Bench 4.1 with its multi-model harness, at 88% lower cost than Claude Fable 5.2 in that comparison. Jay ParikhImage editing. Artificial Analysis ranks MAI Image 2.7 first on its editing benchmark, at $34.82 per 1,000 images. Artificial AnalysisGemini Tasks. Hydrogen now powers free Tasks in six countries, including tasks that need a phone call or a text. Google also showed a new Antigravity robotics plugin with MuJoCo simulation. Sundar Pichai · Google DeepMindAgent harnesses and inferenceHugging Face’s Pi adapter. A small adapter trained inside pi lifted Qwen3.8-27B from 15 to 32 solves on the 51 hardest SWE-bench Pro tasks. Across that subset it made 55% fewer tool calls per task. Model card and paired resultsHarness costs vary sharply. Baseten measured up to a 4.4× spread in cost per passing task across its benchmark of 22 harnesses and five open models. BasetenThe harness may specialize to its model. Google’s SIM keeps the rationale and outcome of prior harness edits. A harness it evolved on Opus scored 68.41 on Gemini, versus 73.89 for the starting harness. Research summaryMore multi-agent products. Cognition launched persistent Devin Bots. Perplexity reported that its mixed-model teams beat four instances of the lead model on Terminal-Bench and WANDR. Replit reported diminishing returns from 16 to 32 agents on NumPy tasks. Cognition · Perplexity · ReplitCoordination dominated a 1,000-agent run. Hugging Face says only 40–60 agents were calling the model at any moment. They read roughly 130 tokens for every token they wrote, with merges and tests contributing to the bottleneck. Thomas WolfA small fraction of cache misses can dominate the bill. SemiAnalysis reports that 1.8% of uncached requests accounted for roughly 15% of spend in its sample. SemiAnalysisMarin and K2 Horizon opened up their training runs. Marin released 57 intermediate Mochi checkpoints from its 535B-A23B run. The K2 report compares four model sizes trained on the same 22T tokens and describes a decoding adapter that the team says reaches 2.2× speedup. Marin · K2 HorizonZyphra’s long-context attention. The team reports 9–60× speedups at 10M tokens after converting several models to its subquadratic attention, with Qwen losing under two points on RULER at 1M. ZyphraSpeculative decoding. vLLM reports up to 30% higher acceptance length from a sliding-window draft for Kimi K3.1 Pro. NVIDIA also has a 4B draft for Qwen3.8-27B. vLLM · Draft-model researchIndustry and policyNVIDIA’s first earnings after the CEO transition. Under interim CEO Colette Kress, NVIDIA posted $115.8B in quarterly revenue, up 103% year over year, and said Vera Rubin NVL72 had shipped. The board said it did not intend to reinstate Jensen Huang. NVIDIA · APIsomorphic Labs raises $5B. Greenoaks and Sequoia co-led the Series C. The company says it will scale its drug-design platform and develop its therapeutic pipeline. Isomorphic LabsGenesis AI raises $500M. The Series A values the robotics company at $3.5B post-money. It plans to use the funding to deploy its Eno robot and expand training and data collection. Zhou XianAI Reddit RecapLocal models and hardwareA 9B model with layers that run twice. SenseNova-Loop-9B runs 24 of its 32 layers a second time. The model’s authors report GAIA rising from 37.86 in the preview to 69.90 in the release. Local users asked how much memory remains for the KV cache at long context. Weights · DiscussionMaxwell V1 Flash. The 35B/3B-active MoE claims a 6.7× attention speedup over dense GQA at 256K. Its sparse attention still retains the full-history KV cache, which is what local users want measured before they commit hardware. Model card · DiscussionOlala mini 7A1B. OVHcloud previewed a small MoE with 1B active parameters and a 32K context window. The thread is waiting for weights and reproducible benchmarks. OVHcloud · DiscussionIntel’s Crescent Island numbers. The early brief’s eye-catching throughput comparison uses FP64-heavy workloads. Intel’s separate LLM comparison claims 1.12× throughput and 29% lower latency versus RTX PRO 6000 Blackwell Server Edition. Hardware discussionGemma on a printer. A builder reports running Gemma 3 270M via a PostScript print job. DemoAgents in useA video-game agent built for real-time input. miHoYo’s Gamer samples the screen at 5 Hz and emits keyboard and mouse activity at 30 Hz. Its RL version solved about half of the held-out Honkai puzzle tasks in the authors’ evaluation. Project · DiscussionA fictional league runs a nightly broadcast. The builder says Fock Ball simulates the games in a physics engine and uses Claude for surrounding work such as commentary and the newsroom. Builder’s postICLR reviews and AI detectors. Reviewers report that the program chairs flagged likely AI-generated reviews. The thread asks how a detector can distinguish editing help from whole-review generation. Peer review discussion
